text:
customer_jess: Hey, our EU customers are seeing 400-800ms extra p99 on every Redwood API call since ~0800 UTC, and sometimes we see requests landing in us-east-1. Ticket #INC-4321.

emma_cs: Thanks for flagging, Jess. Can you paste a raw curl of the failing call + response headers?

customer_jess: Sure. Repro from Frankfurt (client in eu-central-1):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_xxx' \
  -H 'X-Client-Region: eu-central-1' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-1-large","prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response headers snippet: 
```
HTTP/2 200
server: envoy
date: Wed, 10 Feb 2026 08:12:34 GMT
x-served-region: us-east-1
content-length: 1234
```
Body latency ~920ms.

jason_support: Noted. Route header shows x-served-region: us-east-1, which is wrong for eu-central-1 origin. Adding SRE.

sre-bot: Incident INC-4321 created, priority P1, paging oncall.

ingrid_sre: Can you repro with host header and adding X-Region? I want raw proxy logs.

customer_jess: Pasting a request-id: req-9fa3c. I see backend target us-east-1 in our logs too.

mike_runtime: On our side I see an L7 fallback rule in gateway route table that rewrites region header for unmatched cluster affinity. Might be hitting fallback path. Pulling envoy route config from the edge cluster.

jason_support: Do you have the edge config snippet? Also does this affect all customers or only some?

mike_runtime: Only customers pinned to eu-models cluster seem affected intermittently when eu pool is under pressure. Here is the relevant envoy vhost/route fragment we found (anonymized):
```
- match: { prefix: "/v1/" }
  route:
    cluster: "%UPSTREAM_CLUSTER%"
    request_headers_to_add:
      - header:
          key: "x-served-region"
          value: "%ROUTE_REGION%"
    runtime: { key: "fallback.to_default_region", default: true }
```

ingrid_sre: That runtime flag means when cluster selection fails we fall back to default cluster and still set x-served-region from the route template. If cluster selection flips after route resolution, header can be wrong. I want the envoy access logs around req-9fa3c.

jason_support: customer_jess can you share your proxy trace or any Gateway request logs?

customer_jess: Attached trace: shows upstream host 10.240.3.22 (us-east). Start->proxy select EU cluster, but retry path chooses default due to 503 from one EU node, then header doesn't get updated correctly.

mike_runtime: Reproduced locally with a traffic-shift test: if eu pool returns 503 on initial request, Envoy will route to fallback cluster but the templated header value is evaluated earlier and not re-evaluated on retry. So header stays set to the original route template (default region) or sometimes the fallback region depending on order.

ingrid_sre: TL;DR: header eval is happening in route entry evaluation before retry/fallback resolution. That can leak wrong region info to backends and observability, and confuses downstream routing that uses x-served-region for affinity.

emma_cs: Customer impact: higher latency + wrong-region charge and possible data locality concerns. Billing and legal teams flagged.

billing-bot: Created billing case BILL-998 with suggested temporary credits for affected customers.

jason_support: Immediate mitigation options?

mike_runtime: Two quick mitigations: 1) Stop adding x-served-region in the request_headers_to_add at the edge (short-term toggle). 2) Make header add conditional on final upstream selection or use response_headers_to_add on upstream cluster to reflect actual target. I'll prepare a canary change to remove header injection from the edge routing layer.

ingrid_sre: Agreed. Also push a fix to template evaluation ordering so the header is computed from the final cluster at request commit time. That's a runtime patch; schedule for hotfix.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for config change cfg-2026-02-10-01 to cluster edge-eu-canary.

mike_runtime: Canary shows resolve: requests now land in eu cluster and header is either absent (mitigation 1) or correctly set (mitigation 2). p99 back to normal ~120ms.

customer_jess: Confirmed for our EU traffic — latency normalized and x-served-region now eu-central-1. Thank you.

ingrid_sre: We'll ship the header-evaluation fix in runtime 2.7.3 (hotfix) and keep the mitigation toggle for 48h. I'm opening a RFC so we don't template region headers at route-matching time anymore.

jason_support: Action items: 1) document mitigation steps in support KB (I'll write). 2) add regression test in e2e for header correctness on fallback. 3) billing to issue credits.

billing-bot: Billing credit issued: 5% monthly usage credit for affected customers in INC-4321; follow-up email queued.

emma_cs: I'll send a customer update email summary and link to postmortem.

sre-bot: Incident INC-4321 => resolved (mitigation deployed & hotfix scheduled). Closing page.

jason_support: Closing the thread. If anyone sees recurrence, re-open. :thumbsup:
